lines.text: Union is the generous operator. It keeps everything either shape claims
lines.note: union depends on a yes/no crossing test with no middle: at one float the solids are two, at the next they are one — and the seam it advertises as dissolved is the curve it had to compute first.

note_src.quote: CSG union has no k: it fuses absolutely

lines.text: Intersection is the shape of consensus. What both shapes agree on is always less than either …
lines.note: intersection depends on an interior the renderer never draws, and it is the one operator whose lawful answer can be nothing: two solids that miss return the empty solid, indistinguishable from a build that failed.

note_src.quote: the boundary was just the only part that ever got rendered

lines.text: To make a room, subtract a void from a solid. Architecture is difference
lines.note: difference depends on a face neither solid brought: the cavity wall is B inverted, and it can only be dressed in A's outer skin — a boundary model stores no interior, so the carved inside is the outside, relabelled.

note_src.quote: That wall belongs to neither input; it is B's shape, inverted, wearing A's material.

lines.text: Three operators, one algebra. Composition is a choice
lines.note: the bench calls three operators an algebra, but the three are an enum on a Godot property: the set is what the engine exposes, not what the algebra holds — no complement, no XOR, closure bought by leaving them out.

note_src.quote: The set as tooling defines it.

pearls.edge: the chamber's verb is to compose, and composition needs an order the finished solid cannot keep: the block handed back has no memory of which verb came first, so the room depends on you remembering.

edge_src.quote: the order of your verbs matters the way it does in arithmetic

pearls.edge: the map claims a room is a wall subtracted from, but one difference makes a hole, not an inside: an interior needs three more runs of solid the map never places — the payoff is read from outside.

edge_src.quote: never delivers the truth line: a wall has no interior.
